facts.statement: Iyuku is known from a unique bonebed containing at least 27 juvenile and hatchling individuals, a discovery never reported before.
facts.quote: Iykuku is known from a bonebed mostly containing the remains of at least 27 (inferred from non-overlapping parts of the left femora) juvenile and hatchling individuals, an occurrence never before reported.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AM 6067 is an incomplete, semi-articulated skeleton with a partial skull, vertebrae, scapulae, pelvic girdle, legs, and ribs.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, AM 6067, consists of an incomplete, semi-articulated skeleton, including a partial skull, vertebrae, scapulae, pelvic girdle, both legs, and ribs.

facts.statement: The genus name Iyuku comes from the Xhosa word for "hatchling" because the specimens are immature.
facts.quote: The generic name "Iyuku", is derived from the Xhosa word for "hatchling", in reference to the immature status of the specimens.

facts.statement: Iyuku is an iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kirkwood Formation of South Africa.
facts.quote: Iyuku (meaning "hatchling", pronounced "eye-yoo-koo") is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Kirkwood Formation of South Africa.

facts.statement: Iyuku lived during the Early Cretaceous Valanginian, approximately 139 to 132 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Iyuku raathi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Iyuku ("Cría"), un dinosaurio iguanodontiano driosáurido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 139 a 132 millones de años durante el valanginiense, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: Iyuku lived between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago during the Valanginian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Iyuku to the Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: The describers assigned Iyuku to the Iguanodontia.

facts.statement: Later analyses by Poole (2022) recovered Iyuku as the sister taxon to Dysalotosaurus within the family Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Subsequently, four phylogenetic analyses conducted by Poole (2022) recovered Iyuku as the sister taxon to Dysalotosaurus within Dryosauridae.

facts.statement: Fossils from the quarry site consist mostly of isolated bones of hatchlings and juveniles in a 20–30 cm thick horizon with no preferred orientation.
facts.quote: Fossil material from the quarry site includes mostly isolated bones (with only five instances of articulation) of hatchling to juvenile individuals of varying size in a 20–30 cm thick horizon, preserved with no apparent preferred orientation of long bones.

facts.statement: Although no nests were found, researchers suggest the concentration of young individuals may represent seasonal mortality near a nesting site, with bones scattered by trampling or bioturbation.
facts.quote: Although the remains of Iyuku were not found in association with nests or eggshells, Forster et al. (2022) considered it possible that the concentrations of young individuals of this species represent seasonal attrition at or near a nesting site, with the scattering of bones likely caused by trampling prior to burial or bioturbation shortly after interment.

facts.statement: Bone histology shows rest lines indicating temporary growth arrests, hypothesized to be caused by environmental stress like drought or extreme heat.
facts.quote: Bone histology of multiple young individuals reveals rest lines indicative of temporary arrests in bone deposition, hypothesized by Forster et al. (2022) as caused by repeated, possibly environmentally induced stress during the early stages of ontogeny in these individuals, such as dry and drought-like conditions and/or repeated periods of extreme heat.

facts.statement: Iyuku fossils were found in the Kirkwood Formation of the Early Cretaceous in South Africa.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron hallados en la Formación Kirkwood del Cretácico Inferior de Sudáfrica.

facts.statement: Fossils from the quarry site include mostly isolated bones of hatchlings and juveniles in a 20 to 30 cm thick horizon without a preferred orientation.
facts.quote: El material fósil del sitio de la cantera incluye en su mayoría huesos aislados, con solo cinco instancias de articulación, de crías a individuos juveniles de tamaño variable en un horizonte de 20 a 30 cm de espesor, preservados sin una orientación preferida aparente de los huesos largos.

facts.statement: Forster et al. (2022) noted similarities to juvenile remains of Orodromeus, Maiasaura, and Hypacrosaurus, suggesting possible mortality increases near nesting sites.
facts.quote: Forster et al. en 2022 notaron la similitud de este hallazgo con la preservación informada de los restos juveniles de Orodromeus, Maiasaura e Hypacrosaurus, que podrían representar aumentos de la mortalidad cerca de los sitios de anidación.

facts.statement: Bone histology reveals rest lines indicating temporary growth arrests, hypothesized to be caused by repeated environmental stress such as dry conditions or extreme heat.
facts.quote: Histología ósea de múltiples individuos jóvenes revela líneas de descanso indicativas de detenciones temporales en la deposición ósea, según la hipótesis de Forster y colegas como causado por el estrés repetido, posiblemente inducido por el medio ambiente, durante las primeras etapas de la ontogenia en estos individuos, como condiciones secas y similares a la sequía o períodos repetidos de calor extremo.
